reviewMethod: Antigravity drafts separately reviewed against complete archived version bodies and source notes; source discrepancies retained explicitly.

headings.title: Authority to organize districts and construct drainage works
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history/prior-revisions notes (RSMo 1939 §§ 12398, 12452, A. 1949 S.B. 1083). Covers county commission authority, when conducive to public health, convenience, welfare, utility, or benefit, to organize drainage districts and construct or alter ditches, drains, non-navigable natural streams, bank protection, current control, or watercourses to drain or protect land or property.

headings.title: Included lateral works, outlet compensation, and federal consent
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history notes. Covers implied petition scope for side, lateral, spur, or branch works, lake lowering, and bank erosion protection, commission power to establish laterals then or later with outlet compensation to the main ditch district, and the proviso requiring federal consent before actual work on any navigable stream.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read both subsections and history/prior-revisions notes (RSMo 1939 §§ 12398, 12452, A. 1949 S.B. 1083) and verified all source and subsection fingerprints. Checked public health/convenience/welfare/utility conditions, non-navigable natural stream limitation in subsection 1, implied lateral/lake-lowering/bank-protection scope, main-district outlet compensation, and the federal-consent proviso for navigable streams in subsection 2. Retained both drafted titles as accurate.

headings.title: Appointing engineer and viewers, qualifications, quorum, and oath
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history/prior-revisions notes (RSMo 1939 § 12401, A.L. 1990 H.B. 1070). Covers appointment after petition and approved bond of a civil and drainage engineer (individual, copartnership, or corporation) and three Missouri-resident disinterested viewers (not landowners in the proposed district or kin within the fourth degree of consanguinity), viewer majority quorum, and subscribed oath.

headings.title: Preliminary view, necessity report, surveys, and engineering expenses
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history notes. Covers viewing the proposed site and adjacent premises under certified commission order, reporting necessity, practicability, public utility, and approximate character, dimensions, location, and probable cost, and engineer authority to hire assistants, make surveys, and with commission approval secure consulting/expert advice taxed as petition expenses.

headings.title: Report of benefitted adjacent property, boundaries, and maps
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 and history notes. Distinguished from subsection 2 by covering identification and reporting of adjacent benefitted land or property with owner names, expanded district boundary lines, and prompt filing of written findings, maps, profiles, and drawings with the county clerk.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read all three subsections and history/prior-revisions notes (RSMo 1939 § 12401, A.L. 1990 H.B. 1070) and verified all source and subsection fingerprints. Checked appointment after bond approval, civil/drainage engineer entity forms, Missouri-resident disinterested viewer qualifications (fourth-degree consanguinity bar), viewer quorum and oath, preliminary site view and commission-approved consulting expenses, and reporting of benefitted adjacent property and expanded boundaries. Retained all three drafted titles as accurate.

headings.title: Filing and summary hearing of remonstrances
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history/prior-revisions notes (RSMo 1939 § 12403). Covers written remonstrances or objections to the petition or viewers report filed with the county clerk within ten days after the last publication of section 243.060 notice, heard and determined summarily by the county commission.

headings.title: Favorable findings, bond release, and district incorporation
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history notes. Covers mandatory favorable finding when owners of a majority in acreage petition or join, discretionary authority when less than a majority, release of petitioners from bond liability upon a favorable finding, and incorporation of the described property into a numbered drainage district by order of record. Revised during review from 'Majority findings' to cover both mandatory majority-acreage and discretionary less-than-majority favorable findings without ambiguity.

headings.title: Corporate status, powers, and property holding
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 and history notes. Establishes the district as a body corporate and political subdivision with usual public-corporation powers, capacity to sue and be sued, and capacity to hold donated, acquired, or existing real and personal property.

headings.title: Dismissal of petition and itemized cost bill
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 4 and history notes. Covers mandatory dismissal of the petition and proceedings at petitioners cost if the county commission finds against the improvement, with an itemized bill of costs and expenses issued like circuit-clerk fee bills.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read all four subsections and history/prior-revisions notes (RSMo 1939 § 12403) and verified all source and subsection fingerprints. Checked 10-day remonstrance window after section 243.060 publication, mandatory (majority-acreage) vs. discretionary (less-than-majority) favorable findings, petitioner bond release, district incorporation, corporate/political-subdivision status, and dismissal with circuit-clerk-style cost bill. Revised subsection 2 title from 'Majority findings' to 'Favorable findings' to cover both mandatory and discretionary favorable determinations without ambiguity; retained subsections 1, 3, and 4.

headings.title: Locating improvements, surveys, profiles, estimates, and district map
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history/prior-revisions notes (RSMo 1939 § 12405). Covers directing viewers and engineer after district establishment to fix precise improvement locations, dimensions, and form (with permitted line variations, outlet extension, and division-line preference), engineering surveys, profiles, excavation/work estimates, and district mapping.

headings.title: Land-corner witness records and engineering assistants
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history notes. Covers noting and reestablishing land-corner witness marks destroyed by construction, filing a complete record with the county surveyor for recording, and hiring assistants or consulting/expert advice at district expense with commission approval.

headings.title: Schedule and five-column report of benefits and damages
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 and history notes. Covers scheduling tracts of forty acres or less, roads, railroads, and other property benefitted or damaged with owner names, assessing benefits and damages, and reporting findings in the prescribed five-column tabular format.

headings.title: Right-of-way valuations and total cost estimate
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 4 and history notes. Covers describing and valuing land and property inside or outside the district needed for rights-of-way and estimating total cost including organization, damages, property acquisition, and incidental expenses.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read all four subsections and history/prior-revisions notes (RSMo 1939 § 12405) and verified all source and subsection fingerprints. Checked improvement location flexibility, outlet extension, division-line preference, surveys/profiles/estimates/map, destroyed land-corner witness recording with the county surveyor, 40-acre tract scheduling and five-column benefit/damage tabular report, right-of-way valuation inside or outside the district, and total cost estimates. Retained all four drafted titles as accurate.

headings.title: Filing report and cost bill within thirty days
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history/prior-revisions notes (RSMo 1939 § 12406). Requires viewers and engineer to file their section 243.080 report with maps, profiles, schedules, estimates, and itemized cost bill with the county commission clerk within thirty days after completing surveys and estimates.

headings.title: Opportunity for affected landowners to appear before viewers
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history notes. Permits any person whose lands may be affected by the improvement to appear before the viewers and freely express opinions on related matters.

headings.title: Filling vacancies among viewers or engineer
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 and history notes. Authorizes the county commission to appoint a qualified replacement who must take the statutory oath if any engineer or viewer dies or fails or refuses to qualify and serve.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read all three subsections and history/prior-revisions notes (RSMo 1939 § 12406) and verified all source and subsection fingerprints. Checked 30-day filing deadline for the section 243.080 report and itemized cost bill, affected landowners' right to appear before viewers, and county commission replacement and oath requirements for viewer or engineer vacancies. Retained all three drafted titles as accurate.

headings.title: Benefit limits for property not traversed by improvements
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history/prior-revisions notes (RSMo 1939 § 12407). Bars viewers from considering benefits from unbuilt future ditches when assessing non-traversed property, limiting assessment to benefits derived from the district improvements, outlet, or overflow/damage protection.

headings.title: Credit for existing drains, ditches, or levees
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history notes. Directs viewers to give due consideration and credit for previously constructed drains, ditches, or levees affording partial or complete protection to any tract in the new district.

headings.title: Assessing benefits to highways, railroads, and roadways
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 and history notes. Establishes the assessment basis for public highways, railroads, rights-of-way, roadways, and other property according to increased physical efficiency and decreased roadway maintenance cost.

headings.title: Assessing remaining acreage after partial tract acquisition
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 4 and history notes. Requires viewers to list the remainder of any partially acquired tract in the benefit schedule, show remaining acreage, and estimate benefits accruing to the remainder.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read all four subsections and history/prior-revisions notes (RSMo 1939 § 12407) and verified all source and subsection fingerprints. Checked exclusion of unbuilt future ditches for non-traversed property, credit for existing drains/ditches/levees, efficiency/maintenance assessment standard for highways and railroads, and remainder-acreage benefit listing after partial tract acquisition. Retained all four drafted titles as accurate.

headings.title: Filing, hearing, and confirmation after exceptions
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history/prior-revisions notes (RSMo 1939 § 12409). Covers exceptions filed by the district attorney or property owners within ten days after last publication of section 243.110 notice, summary commission determination, and confirmation of the modified report if estimated construction cost is less than assessed benefits.

headings.title: Exception costs and condemnation of needed property
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history notes. Covers adjudging and apportioning exception costs and condemning needed property inside or outside the district for rights-of-way, holding basins, works, or materials following telegraph, telephone, and railroad condemnation procedures as nearly as possible.

headings.title: Payment before entry, five-year abatement, and vesting
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 and history notes. Requires cash payment of property price and damages before entry or appropriation, abates unpaid taking proceedings at district cost after five years from final confirmation, and vests title, use, possession, and disposition in the district upon payment.

headings.title: Right and scope of circuit court appeal
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 4 including subdivisions (1) and (2) and history notes. Authorizes circuit court appeal from the county commission judgment limited to determining just compensation for appropriated property and/or proper damages for prejudicially affected property.

headings.title: Verified appeal application deadline and recording
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 5 and history notes. Conditions granting the appeal on filing a verified written application specifying matters appealed before the end of the commission term and within ten days of the order, recorded on commission records.

headings.title: Appeal bond, transcript, no stay, and amended-report notice
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 6 including the multi-row statutory notice table (block 17) and history notes. Covers fixing and ten-day filing of the appeal bond with two freehold sureties, ten-day transcript certification to circuit court, the non-stay rule allowing construction to proceed, and optional referral back to viewers with new section 243.110 notice in prescribed form.

headings.title: Exceptions and proceedings on amended reports
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 7 and history notes. Applies the same filing deadlines, manner, and subsequent proceedings to exceptions against an amended report as to the original report.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read all seven subsections including subdivisions (1)-(2) in subsection 4, the embedded multi-row statutory notice form table in subsection 6 (div block 17), and history/prior-revisions notes (RSMo 1939 § 12409), and verified all source and subsection fingerprints. Checked 10-day section 243.110 exception window, cost-less-than-benefits confirmation condition, condemnation procedure, cash-before-entry and five-year abatement rules, narrow two-issue circuit court appeal scope, verified 10-day appeal application, 10-day appeal bond and transcript certification, non-stay proviso, referral back to viewers with statutory amended-report notice form, and amended-report exceptions. Retained all seven drafted titles as accurate.

headings.title: Deemed inclusion application and filing of benefit record
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history/prior-revisions notes (RSMo 1939 § 12445). Treats outside land whose owner connects to a district ditch or drain or whose land is or will be benefitted as having made voluntary application for inclusion, and directs the county commission to obtain and file benefit descriptions, owner names, and connecting-ditch descriptions.

headings.title: Hearing notice, annexation decision, and maintenance assessment
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history notes. Retains source text "to such owner or owners of, if a nonresident, to his tenant" ("of" for "or" in source). Covers setting a complaint hearing at least fifteen days after filing, ten days written notice served on the owner or nonresident tenant proven by affidavit, rendering and filing the annexation decision, and assessing annexed land for maintenance.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read both subsections and history/prior-revisions notes (RSMo 1939 § 12445) and verified all source and subsection fingerprints. Checked deemed voluntary inclusion for connecting or benefitted outside land, benefit/connection record filing, 15-day hearing floor, 10-day written notice proven by affidavit (retaining source typo 'owner or owners of, if a nonresident'), annexation decision filing, and maintenance assessment. Retained both drafted titles as accurate.

headings.title: Authority to construct confirmed district improvements
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history/prior-revisions notes (RSMo 1939 § 12423). Grants the county commission full power on behalf of a drainage district to build, construct, excavate, and complete works described in the confirmed viewers and engineer report.

headings.title: Direct construction by commission labor and machinery
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history notes. Distinguished from subsection 3 by empowering the commission to employ workers and teams, rent or purchase machinery, and directly construct improvements or use other or more efficient means than adopted plans.

headings.title: Letting construction contracts and published notice
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 and history notes. Distinguished from subsection 2 by authorizing discretionary contract letting as a whole or in sections and requiring published notice in three consecutive issues of a county weekly newspaper and at least one contractor or trade journal insertion at least ten days before letting.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read all three subsections and history/prior-revisions notes (RSMo 1939 § 12423) and verified all source and subsection fingerprints. Checked county commission construction power for confirmed plans, direct force-account labor/machinery authority, and discretionary contract letting with three-week county newspaper and 10-day-prior trade-journal notice. Retained all three drafted titles as accurate.

headings.title: Appointment of district engineer and approved assistants
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history/prior-revisions notes (RSMo 1939 § 12424, A.L. 1990 H.B. 1070). Requires appointment of a competent civil and drainage engineer (individual, copartnership, or corporation) within sixty days after report confirmation, with commission-approved assistants.

headings.title: Engineering control, construction supervision, and annual reports
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history notes. Covers district engineer control over engineering work, optional commission-approved consulting engineer, construction superintendence, and full reports and recommendations when required and at least once annually.

headings.title: District engineer performance bond requirements
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 and history notes. Requires a performance bond of at least $1,000 (or greater fixed by the commission), signed by at least two county residents or an authorized surety company, payable to the district and preserved in the county clerk office.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read all three subsections and history/prior-revisions notes (RSMo 1939 § 12424, A.L. 1990 H.B. 1070) and verified all source and subsection fingerprints. Checked 60-day post-confirmation appointment of district engineer (individual/copartnership/corporation) and approved assistants, engineering control, optional consulting engineer, construction superintendence and annual reports, and $1,000-minimum performance bond preserved by the county clerk. Retained all three drafted titles as accurate.

headings.title: Offering working sections and announcing contract terms
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history/prior-revisions notes (RSMo 1939 § 12425). Directs the district engineer to let or offer to let working-section construction as ordered by the county commission, announcing terms and completion time.

headings.title: Bidder performance bonds and engineer return of contracts
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history notes. Requires successful bidders to deliver a performance bond of at least twenty percent of the bid to the engineer, and requires the engineer to return all contracts and bonds and file a proceedings report with the county clerk within fifteen days after bids are received.

headings.title: Commission approval, recording, and time extensions
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 and history notes. Covers commission approval or rejection on record with notice to contractors, clerk filing and drainage-record recording of bonds and duplicate contracts, and discretionary good-cause time extensions that do not impair the contract or release sureties.

headings.title: Reletting unperformed work and defaulting contractor liability
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 4 and history notes. Authorizes reletting unperformed work in the original manner (barring a second letting to the same person) and makes the defaulting contractor liable on bond for resulting damages, costs, and expenses.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read all four subsections and history/prior-revisions notes (RSMo 1939 § 12425) and verified all source and subsection fingerprints. Checked engineer offering working sections, 20-percent bidder performance bond and 15-day return/report deadline, commission record approval/rejection, clerk filing and drainage-record recording, non-impairing good-cause time extensions, reletting prohibition against the same contractor, and defaulting-contractor bond liability. Retained all four drafted titles as accurate.

headings.title: Bridge or culvert construction and corporate owner assessments
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history/prior-revisions notes (RSMo 1939 § 12427). Authorizes necessary bridge or culvert construction or enlargement across district ditches, and sets notice, refusal, twenty-day pre-letting notice, cost assessment, and tax-lien collection procedures when owned by a corporation other than the county.

headings.title: Highway bridges transferred to road maintenance authority
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history notes. Retains source adverb phrasing "adjudged sufficiently by the county commission". Provides that a ditch bridge crossing a public highway and so adjudged becomes part of the highway maintained, repaired, or replaced by the road maintenance authority.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read both subsections and history/prior-revisions notes (RSMo 1939 § 12427) and verified all source and subsection fingerprints. Checked bridge/culvert construction or enlargement authority, non-county corporate-owner notice/refusal, 20-day actual pre-letting notice, tax-lien cost assessment, and highway transfer for ditch bridges 'adjudged sufficiently' (source phrasing retained) by the county commission. Retained both drafted titles as accurate.

headings.title: Landowner statement requesting repairs or new work
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history/prior-revisions notes (RSMo 1939 § 12435). Permits five or more originally assessed landowners to file a written statement with the county clerk when district ditches or improvements need enlarging, cleaning, obstruction removal, or new work.

headings.title: Engineer inspection and written cost report
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history notes. Retains source spelling "ditch, drain or levy" ("levy" for "levee"). Directs the county commission at its next meeting to order the district or selected engineer to view the premises and report necessary repairs, improvements, and probable restoration cost.

headings.title: Commission order for maintenance-fund repairs
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 and history notes. Covers prompt commission consideration of the engineer report and ordering recommended repairs and improvements—including supplies, labor, and itemized reporting—paid from the district maintenance fund.

headings.title: Partial work and notice form for excess-cost tax hearing
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 4 including the multi-row statutory notice table (block 9) and history notes. Retains source phrasing "it should be the duty". Covers ordering repairs affordable from the maintenance fund when needed work exceeds available funds, setting an additional-tax hearing for the first day of the next regular term, and publishing notice in three issues of a county weekly newspaper in prescribed form.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read all four subsections including the embedded multi-row statutory notice form table in subsection 4 (div block 9) and history/prior-revisions notes (RSMo 1939 § 12435), and verified all source and subsection fingerprints. Checked five-landowner written statement, engineer inspection and restoration cost report (retaining source spelling 'ditch, drain or levy'), maintenance-fund repair orders, and excess-cost partial-work/additional-tax hearing notice form (retaining source phrasing 'it should be the duty'). Retained all four drafted titles as accurate.

headings.title: Summary hearing, majority-acreage finding, and cost investigation
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history/prior-revisions notes (RSMo 1939 § 12436, A.L. 1945 p. 858). Covers summary hearing on the section 243.220 statement, mandatory favorable finding if owners of a majority in acreage signed or joined, and ordering the district or county highway engineer to investigate and report restoration cost.

headings.title: Applying maintenance funds and levying pro rata deficiency tax
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history notes. Covers deducting available maintenance funds from estimated cost plus ten percent for emergencies (appropriating those funds if approved), dividing any deficiency plus ten percent pro rata by original assessed benefits, placing the tax on tax books, and optionally allowing up to five annual installments.

headings.title: Work supervision, section 243.330 machinery, accounting, and review
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 and history notes. Covers engineer supervision, progress statements, and maintenance-fund warrants, pre-payment estimates and fund transfers for rental or repair/depreciation and removal of section 243.330 dredge boats, tools, or machinery, permanent strict cost accounting, and review of commission orders as otherwise provided by law.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read all three subsections and history/prior-revisions notes (RSMo 1939 § 12436, A.L. 1945 p. 858) and verified all source and subsection fingerprints. Checked summary hearing on section 243.220 statements, mandatory majority-acreage finding, maintenance-fund deduction plus 10-percent emergency reserve and pro rata deficiency tax (up to five installments), engineer supervision, section 243.330 machinery rental/depreciation/removal transfers, strict permanent cost accounting, and order review. Retained all three drafted titles as accurate.

headings.title: County commission duty to manage and maintain districts
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history/prior-revisions notes (RSMo 1939 § 12433). Places continuous management, control, and duty to maintain district efficiency—maintaining, preserving, restoring, repairing, strengthening, and replacing drains, ditches, and levees—on county commissions.

headings.title: Administering county districts as one maintenance unit
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history notes. Permits treating and administering all drainage districts in a county as a single maintenance unit under sections 243.220 to 243.240, 243.280, 243.330, and 243.380 upon petition by a majority of landowners owning a majority of acres in each district.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read both subsections and history/prior-revisions notes (RSMo 1939 § 12433) and verified all source and subsection fingerprints. Checked continuous county commission management and maintenance duty in subsection 1 and permissive county-wide single-unit maintenance administration upon majority-landowner/majority-acreage petitions from each district under sections 243.220 to 243.240, 243.280, 243.330, and 243.380 in subsection 2. Retained both drafted titles as accurate.

headings.title: Permitted lateral connections and box or tiling requirements
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1, history/prior-revisions notes (RSMo 1939 § 12442), and case annotation (1958, Rice v. Stoddard, 312 S.W.2d 374, regarding private-levee surface water entering a district watercourse via steel tubing). Permits persons or corporations to connect lateral ditches or drains into district works only through intersection boxes or tiling as large as the lateral ditch and at least fifteen feet long.

headings.title: Misdemeanor offense for violations
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2, history notes, and Rice v. Stoddard annotation. Declares all persons violating section 243.250 guilty of a misdemeanor without specifying a separate fine or jail range. Revised during review from 'Misdemeanor penalty' to 'Misdemeanor offense' for precision.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read both subsections, history/prior-revisions notes (RSMo 1939 § 12442), and the 1958 case annotation (Rice v. Stoddard, 312 S.W.2d 374, addressing surface water from a private levee entering a district watercourse via steel tubing), and verified all source and subsection fingerprints. Checked conditional lateral-connection permission requiring full-width intersection boxes or tiling at least 15 feet long, and misdemeanor classification in subsection 2. Revised subsection 2 title from 'Misdemeanor penalty' to 'Misdemeanor offense' because no fine/imprisonment range is stated; retained subsection 1.

headings.title: Preliminary per-acre tax levy, delinquency, lien, and collection
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history/prior-revisions notes (RSMo 1939 § 12404). Directs the county commission upon incorporation under sections 243.020 to 243.070 to levy a uniform tax up to fifty cents per acre for preliminary organization, survey, and assessment expenses, due when assessed, delinquent after December 31 of the levy year, operating as a lien, and collected like annual drainage tax installments.

headings.title: Use of tax surplus and refunds for unbenefitted tracts
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history notes. Places any preliminary tax surplus in the district general fund for construction, subject to the proviso requiring a refund warrant for tracts shown by the confirmed viewers report not to be benefitted.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read both subsections and history/prior-revisions notes (RSMo 1939 § 12404) and verified all source and subsection fingerprints. Checked uniform preliminary tax up to 50 cents per acre after incorporation under sections 243.020 to 243.070, immediate due date, December 31 delinquency, lien and collection parity, construction use of surplus, and refund-warrant proviso for unbenefitted tracts. Retained both drafted titles as accurate.

headings.title: Tax levy on assessed benefits plus emergency reserve
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history/prior-revisions notes (RSMo 1939 § 12412). Requires the county commission immediately after confirming the viewers report to levy a tax on assessed benefits necessary for improvement completion and incidental expenses plus ten percent for emergencies.

headings.title: Proportional apportionment and treatment of bond interest
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history notes. Requires proportional apportionment not exceeding assessed benefits, adds estimated bond interest to the tax if bonds are issued, and excludes bond interest from construction cost when comparing expenses against assessed benefits.

headings.title: Optional collection in up to twenty annual installments
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 and history notes. Authorizes the county commission, if deemed advisable, by record order to collect levied taxes in up to twenty annual installments payable and collected with state and county taxes. Revised during review to preserve permissive authority ('Optional collection').

headings.title: County clerk schedule and statutory drainage tax record form
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 4 including the multi-row Drainage Tax Record form table (block 9) and history notes. Directs the county clerk at district expense to prepare the tax list and schedule in substantially the prescribed form, including columns, installment schedule, September 1 certification notice, and lien priority text.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read all four subsections including the embedded multi-row Drainage Tax Record statutory form table in subsection 4 (div block 9) and history/prior-revisions notes (RSMo 1939 § 12412), and verified all source and subsection fingerprints. Checked post-confirmation benefit tax levy plus 10-percent emergency reserve, proportional cap and bond-interest exclusion from construction-cost comparison, permissive up-to-20-installment collection, and clerk preparation of the prescribed Drainage Tax Record form with five columns, September 1 certification text, and lien priority clause. Revised subsection 3 title to 'Optional collection in up to twenty annual installments' to preserve permissive wording; retained subsections 1, 2, and 4.

headings.title: Bound permanent drainage tax record book
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history/prior-revisions notes (RSMo 1939 § 12413). Requires the section 243.300 list and schedule to be prepared in a well-bound endorsed book signed by the county clerk with commission seal and kept as a permanent clerk record.

headings.title: Additional tax levies to complete improvements
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history notes. Directs additional tax levies if proceeds are insufficient to complete confirmed improvements, subject to the proviso that aggregate levies excluding bond-interest taxes do not exceed total assessed and confirmed benefits.

headings.title: Tax levies to pay judgments against district
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 and history notes. Distinguished from subsection 2 by requiring tax levies at the next term after filing a certified copy of a judgment against the district to pay the judgment and interest, apportioned proportionally without exceeding confirmed benefits when combined with other lawful levies.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read all three subsections and history/prior-revisions notes (RSMo 1939 § 12413) and verified all source and subsection fingerprints. Checked well-bound permanent clerk Drainage Tax Record book for section 243.300 schedules, additional completion levies capped at total confirmed benefits excluding bond-interest taxes, and next-term judgment-and-interest levies capped at confirmed benefits combined with other lawful levies. Retained all three drafted titles as accurate.

headings.title: Annual maintenance tax levy, cap, and collection
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history/prior-revisions notes (RSMo 1939 § 12434, A.L. 1953 p. 547). Retains source verb "reserve" in "maintain, reserve, restore, repair, strengthen and replace". Covers the annual May-term maintenance tax apportioned by original construction benefits, capped at ten percent of original construction cost per year, entered separately in ditch tax books, and collected with annual-installment delinquency penalties.

headings.title: Maintenance fund ownership and shared machinery fund apportionment
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history notes. Declares maintenance tax revenues absolute district property credited to the maintenance fund, except for optional county commission set-asides on request into a shared dredge-boat, tool, and machinery purchase fund apportioned half by original benefit-assessment ratio and half by original excavation-yardage ratio.

headings.title: Ownership and use of shared maintenance machinery
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 and history notes. Designates purchased machinery as general property of participating districts used under commission direction to clean and restore works, with a proviso preserving authority to maintain district works using maintenance funds without purchasing machinery.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read all three subsections and history/prior-revisions notes (RSMo 1939 § 12434, A.L. 1953 p. 547) and verified all source and subsection fingerprints. Checked annual May-term maintenance tax (retaining source verb 'reserve' in 'maintain, reserve, restore, repair, strengthen and replace'), 10-percent original-cost annual cap, district ownership of maintenance revenues, optional shared machinery-purchase fund apportioned half by original benefit assessments and half by original excavation yardage, and proviso preserving maintenance without machinery purchases. Retained all three drafted titles as accurate.

headings.title: Annual clerk apportionment of installment and maintenance taxes
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history/prior-revisions notes (RSMo 1939 § 12415, A.L. 1953 p. 538, A.L. 2017 S.B. 112). Requires the county clerk each year to apportion due annual installments and any maintenance taxes against district property in proportion to assessed benefits.

headings.title: Drainage tax book format and required columns
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 including subdivisions (1) through (7) and history notes. Directs the clerk to extend apportioned installment and maintenance taxes into an endorsed well-bound Drainage Tax Book containing seven specified owner, description, tax, collection, payment-date, and payer columns.

headings.title: Delivery of drainage tax book and collection timing
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 and history notes. Requires delivery of the drainage tax book to the county or township collector by September 30 each year, with taxes due and collected alongside state and county taxes.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read all three subsections including subdivisions (1)-(7) of subsection 2 and history/prior-revisions notes (RSMo 1939 § 12415, A.L. 1953 p. 538, A.L. 2017 S.B. 112), and verified all source and subsection fingerprints. Checked annual clerk apportionment of installments and maintenance taxes, seven-column bound Drainage Tax Book format (including township endorsement language), and September 30 delivery deadline to the county or township collector. Retained all three drafted titles as accurate.

headings.title: Collector duty to receive book and collect taxes
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history/prior-revisions notes (RSMo 1939 § 12416, A.L. 1990 H.B. 1070). Requires the county collector of revenue to receive the drainage tax book annually and promptly, faithfully, and diligently collect listed taxes.

headings.title: Collection timing, divided tracts, authority, and accounting
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history notes. Requires demanding and collecting drainage taxes with state and county taxes, accepting partial-tract payments for divided/transferred parcels with receipts, establishes the drainage tax book as collection warrant, and requires annual remittance and accounting to the county treasurer.

headings.title: Collector bond requirements and premium payment
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 and history notes. Requires a collector bond payable to the drainage district for probable yearly drainage taxes, signed by at least two county residents or an authorized surety company and approved by the county commission, with permissive premium payment from district funds.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read all three subsections and history/prior-revisions notes (RSMo 1939 § 12416, A.L. 1990 H.B. 1070) and verified all source and subsection fingerprints. Checked annual collector receipt and collection duties, simultaneous collection with state/county taxes, partial-tract payments on divided/transferred parcels, tax-book warrant authority, annual treasurer accounting, and commission-approved collector bond with permissive district premium payment. Retained all three drafted titles as accurate.

headings.title: Drainage tax lien scope, priority, and collection
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1, history/prior-revisions notes (RSMo 1939 § 12417), and cross-reference note (section 140.380 redemption of delinquent land). Makes chapter drainage and maintenance taxes, penalties, collection costs, and court-fixed attorney fees a lien from levy date until paid, subordinate only to general state, county, school, and road tax liens, collected like real estate taxes.

headings.title: Delinquency date and monthly interest rate
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history/cross-reference notes. Sets delinquency after December 31 of the levy year and imposes one percent monthly interest until paid, counting fractional months as full months.

headings.title: Circuit court enforcement suits on delinquent tax bills
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 and history/cross-reference notes. Covers enforcing liens by circuit court action on collector-certified delinquent tax bills regardless of amount within six months after December 31, brought by the district attorney in the name and to the use of the county collector against the property.

headings.title: Court procedures, sheriff sales, deeds, and tax book effect
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 4 and history/cross-reference notes. Incorporates general delinquent real-estate tax procedures and sheriff sales except as provided, gives sheriff deeds the same probative force, permits the same abbreviations, and gives the drainage tax book the same probative effect as a back tax bill.

headings.title: Post-sale installment liens, suit fees, and sale proceeds
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 5 and history/cross-reference notes. Keeps title acquired at sale subject to subsequent annual drainage tax installments, includes suit costs and court-fixed reasonable attorney fees in judgments, and requires immediate payment of sale proceeds to the county treasurer.

headings.title: Drainage tax books as prima facie evidence
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 6 and history/cross-reference notes. Makes district drainage tax books prima facie evidence in all courts of all matters contained therein.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read all six subsections, history/prior-revisions notes (RSMo 1939 § 12417), and cross-reference note (section 140.380 delinquent-land redemption), and verified all source and subsection fingerprints. Checked tax lien scope and priority subordinate only to state/county/school/road taxes, December 31 delinquency and 1-percent monthly interest (fractional months counted full), six-month circuit court enforcement suits regardless of claim amount, general real-estate tax procedures/sheriff deeds/back-tax-bill effect, survival of subsequent installment liens and judgment fees, and prima facie evidentiary status of drainage tax books. Retained all six drafted titles as accurate.

headings.title: Bond issuance authority and aggregate par-value limit
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1, history/prior-revisions notes (RSMo 1939 § 12418), and cross-reference notes (sections 108.180 to 108.210, 108.230; 108.140 to 108.160). Authorizes county commission bond issuance on behalf of a district to pay confirmed improvement and incidental costs, capping aggregate par value at levied improvement/expense taxes excluding the ten-percent emergency reserve and bond-interest levy.

headings.title: Bond denominations, interest, execution, and maturity limits
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history/cross-reference notes. Specifies $100-multiple denominations, maximum six-percent semiannual interest, payment at the county treasurer office, execution by presiding commissioner and attested clerk with seal, annual maturities starting within five years of first delivery for value, and a twenty-year maturity ceiling.

headings.title: Bond sale, validity, payment, and tax appropriation
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 and history/cross-reference notes. Covers delivery to and sale by the county treasurer with commission approval at not less than ninety-five percent of par plus accrued interest, validity despite signing-official turnover, face-of-bond purpose statement, tax-proceeds payment, installment scheduling, and exclusive dedication of appropriated taxes. Revised during review to avoid conflating appropriated tax proceeds with bond-sale proceeds.

headings.title: Additional levies, nonimpairment of security, and past-due interest
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 4 and history/cross-reference notes. Requires rearranging installment schedules and making additional levies if needed for prompt bond payment, bars any levy impairing bond security or the payment fund, and sets six-percent annual interest on unpaid matured bonds and coupons.

headings.title: Special depositaries and security for bond proceeds
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 5 and history/cross-reference notes. Retains archaic source spelling "especial depositary". Permits record-order selection of temporary-treasurer special depositaries to hold and disburse bond proceeds to the county treasurer as work progresses, secured by approved collateral or Missouri-authorized surety bonds whose premiums may be paid from district funds.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read all five subsections, history/prior-revisions notes (RSMo 1939 § 12418), and cross-reference notes (sections 108.180 to 108.210, 108.230; 108.140 to 108.160), and verified all source and subsection fingerprints. Checked bond par-value ceiling excluding emergency and bond-interest taxes, $100-multiple denominations, 6-percent semiannual interest, 5-year start and 20-year maturity cap, 95-percent minimum sale price, signing-official turnover validity, dedicated tax appropriation, additional levies and nonimpairment rule, 6-percent past-due interest, and temporary-treasurer special depositaries (retaining archaic source spelling 'especial depositary'). Revised subsection 3 title to 'Bond sale, validity, payment, and tax appropriation' to avoid conflating appropriated tax proceeds with bond-sale proceeds; retained subsections 1-2 and 4-5.

headings.title: Authority to pledge section 243.390 and refunding bonds
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history note (RSMo 1939 § 12419). Authorizes the county commission to pledge section 243.390 bonds or refunding bonds to any federal or Missouri corporation, commission, or agency authorized to accept them, conforming to its requirements, rules, or regulations.

headings.title: Redemption funding and lien enforcement for pledged bonds
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history note. Requires providing redemption funds and interest and enforcing the lien of pledged bonds in the same manner as for sold bonds under chapter 243.

headings.title: Deposit, accounting, and expenditure of pledged-bond funds
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 and history note. Directs that funds derived from pledged bonds be deposited, accounted for, and expended either as if sold or per the pledgee agency requirements, rules, or regulations.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read all three subsections and history note (RSMo 1939 § 12419) and verified all source and subsection fingerprints. Checked county commission authority to pledge section 243.390 or refunding bonds to federal or Missouri corporations/commissions/agencies per agency rules, equivalent redemption funding and lien enforcement, and deposit/accounting/expenditure of pledged-bond funds. Retained all three drafted titles as accurate.

headings.title: County treasurer as custodian of district funds
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history/prior-revisions notes (RSMo 1939 § 12422, A.L. 1990 H.B. 1070). Designates the county treasurer as district treasurer and fund custodian, qualified by "except as otherwise provided in this chapter".

headings.title: Receipts and separate district bonds of treasurer
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history notes. Requires receiving and receipting for funds and giving a separate commission-approved bond per district (at least probable funds held at one time, signed by two county residents or an authorized surety company) conditioned on faithful prompt disbursement, with permissive district payment of premiums.

headings.title: Deposit of district funds, interest, and surety premiums
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 and history notes. Requires depositing district funds in bank(s) selected like county depositaries (except as otherwise provided in chapter 243), credits accruing interest to the district, and permits district payment of surety bond premiums.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read all three subsections and history/prior-revisions notes (RSMo 1939 § 12422, A.L. 1990 H.B. 1070) and verified all source and subsection fingerprints. Checked county treasurer designation as district fund custodian ('except as otherwise provided in this chapter'), receipts and separate per-district bonds with permissive district premium payment, county-depositary bank selection, interest crediting, and surety premium payment. Retained all three drafted titles as accurate.

headings.title: Commission determination of fees for district services
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history/prior-revisions notes (RSMo 1939 § 12450, A.L. 1983 H.B. 236). Provides that the county commission determines fees allowed for services actually rendered to chapter 243 drainage districts.

headings.title: Service contracts and vouchers for expense accounts
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history notes. Empowers the county commission to contract for such services and requires all expense accounts to be accompanied by vouchers showing items actually paid.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read both subsections and history/prior-revisions notes (RSMo 1939 § 12450, A.L. 1983 H.B. 236) and verified all source and subsection fingerprints. Checked county commission determination of fees for services actually rendered, contracting power, and mandatory vouchers showing items actually paid on all expense accounts. Retained both drafted titles as accurate.

headings.title: Consolidation petition under sections 242.010 to 242.690
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 including subdivisions (1) through (10) and history/prior-revisions notes (RSMo 1939 § 12446, A.L. 1963 p. 394, A.L. 1986 S.B. 488). Covers petitioning the circuit court of the greatest-acreage county by owners of one-fourth of proposed consolidated acres to bring two or more chapter 243 districts or portions under sections 242.010 to 242.690, stating ten required items covering names, boundaries, acreages, benefits, bonds, and duration.

headings.title: Prayer for corporate status, duration, and consolidated name
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history notes. Requires the petition to request circuit court adjudication as a body corporate for years not exceeding the stated term under the prescribed Consolidated Drainage District name format.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read both subsections including subdivisions (1)-(10) of subsection 1 and history/prior-revisions notes (RSMo 1939 § 12446, A.L. 1963 p. 394, A.L. 1986 S.B. 488), and verified all source and subsection fingerprints. Checked one-fourth acreage petition threshold to reorganize/consolidate chapter 243 districts or portions under sections 242.010 to 242.690 in the greatest-acreage county circuit court, all ten required petition items, and the subsection 2 prayer for corporate status, duration, and Consolidated Drainage District name. Retained both drafted titles as accurate.

headings.title: Publication and form of consolidation hearing notice
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 including the multi-row statutory notice table (block 3) and history/effective-date notes (RSMo 1939 § 12447, A.L. 1978 H.B. 1634, Effective 1-2-79). Directs the circuit clerk of the greatest-acreage county upon petition filing to publish notice for three consecutive weeks (three times) in a newspaper in each affected county in substantially the prescribed form.

headings.title: Original and exclusive multi-county circuit court jurisdiction
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history notes. Grants the circuit court where the petition is filed original and exclusive jurisdiction for chapter purposes coextensive with district boundaries regardless of county lines.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read both subsections including the embedded multi-row statutory notice form table in subsection 1 (div block 3) and history/effective-date notes (RSMo 1939 § 12447, A.L. 1978 H.B. 1634, Effective 1-2-79), and verified all source and subsection fingerprints. Checked three-consecutive-week (three-time) newspaper publication in each affected county in prescribed statutory form and original, exclusive multi-county circuit court jurisdiction coextensive with district boundaries. Retained both drafted titles as accurate.

headings.title: Deadline for non-signing owners to file objections
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history/prior-revisions notes (RSMo 1939 § 12448). Requires any non-signing real estate or property owner objecting to consolidated district organization and incorporation to file objections on or before the first day of the hearing term.

headings.title: Summary hearing, acreage thresholds, verification, withdrawal, and amendments
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history notes. Limits objections to petition denials heard summarily, requires granting if majority-acreage owners signed (or discretionary if less than half), makes a verified petition prima facie evidence, restricts signer withdrawal without majority-acreage signer consent, and permits pleading amendments.

headings.title: Filing decree and plat with state and counties
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 and history notes. Requires circuit clerk transmittal of certified incorporation findings and decree to the secretary of state within sixty days, plus permanent filing of findings, decree, and plat with each affected county recorder for a one-dollar fee.

headings.title: Proceedings under 242.010 to 242.690 and cumulative construction
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 4 and history notes. Directs subsequent proceedings under sections 242.010 to 242.690 and declares chapter 243 cumulative to, rather than conflicting with or repealing, other levee or drainage district incorporation laws. Revised during review to retain the exact statutory cross-reference range '242.010 to 242.690'.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read all four subsections and history/prior-revisions notes (RSMo 1939 § 12448) and verified all source and subsection fingerprints. Checked first-day-of-term objection deadline for non-signing owners, narrow denial-only objections, mandatory majority-acreage vs. discretionary less-than-half granting, verified-petition prima facie evidence, signer-withdrawal restriction, pleading amendments, 60-day secretary-of-state transmittal and $1 county-recorder plat filings, exact sections 242.010 to 242.690 continuation, and cumulative construction. Revised subsection 4 title to preserve the exact statutory range '242.010 to 242.690'; retained subsections 1-3.

headings.title: Petition to consolidate chapter 243 and 242 districts
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 including subdivisions (1) through (7) and notes (L. 1985 H.B. 660 § 1, A.L. 1986 S.B. 488; original-rolls note `*Word "demonstrations" appears in original rolls.` on "denominations*" in subdivision (6); source wording "body corporation" in subdivision (7)). Covers majority-acreage landowner petitions from both a chapter 243 district and a chapter 242 district to consolidate under sections 242.010 to 242.690, listing seven required petition contents and corporate-name request.

headings.title: Notice, objections, order, debt allocation, supervisors, and filings
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 including subdivisions (1) through (3) and history notes. Covers section 242.030 circuit clerk notice, landowner objections by hearing date, consolidation order with sections 242.010 to 242.690 powers, preservation of original liens with outstanding pre-consolidation bond taxes confined to original-district property, election of a new board of supervisors, and court-record/recorder/secretary-of-state filings. Revised during review to explicitly reflect board of supervisors election in subdivision (2).

headings.title: County recorder filing fee for consolidation orders
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 and history notes. Sets a one-dollar fee for each county recorder of deeds to file and preserve each certified copy of orders described in subsection 2(3).

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read all three subsections including subdivisions (1)-(7) and continuation div block 15 in subsection 1, subdivisions (1)-(3) in subsection 2, and all notes (L. 1985 H.B. 660 § 1, A.L. 1986 S.B. 488; original-rolls footnote `*Word "demonstrations" appears in original rolls.` on `denominations*` in subsection 1(6); source wording 'body corporation' in subsection 1 continuation paragraph), and verified all source and subsection fingerprints. Checked dual majority-acreage petitions, section 242.030 notice, pre-consolidation bond debt isolation to original-district property, new board of supervisors election, court/recorder/secretary-of-state filings, and $1 recorder fee. Revised subsection 2 title to explicitly include supervisors election under subdivision (2); retained subsections 1 and 3.

headings.title: Preservation of prior rights, pending actions, and contracts
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history/prior-revisions notes (RSMo 1939 § 12454). Preserves existing drainage district rights, powers, remedies, and liens, pending state and federal court proceedings, and existing obligations, contracts, and undertakings against impairment by the repeal of article 4, chapter 41, RSMo 1909, and existing laws.

headings.title: Elective enforcement under chapter and liberal remedial construction
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history notes. Permits existing drainage districts to elect enforcement of existing rights, powers, liens, and remedies under chapter 243 if applicable, and declares the chapter remedial and subject to liberal judicial construction.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read both subsections and history/prior-revisions notes (RSMo 1939 § 12454) and verified all source and subsection fingerprints. Checked savings clause preserving prior rights, powers, remedies, liens, pending state/federal proceedings, and contracts despite repeal of article 4, chapter 41, RSMo 1909 and existing laws, plus elective chapter 243 enforcement and liberal remedial construction. Retained both drafted titles as accurate.

headings.title: Bond authorization, amount cap, terms, and execution
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history note (L. 1993 S.B. 56 § 243.560 subsecs. 1, 2). Retains source wording "convenient banking hours or trust company's office" ("hours" for "house"). Authorizes county commission bond issuance on a district behalf up to ninety percent of sections 243.550 to 243.553 assessments, in denominations of at least $100, maximum six-percent semiannual interest, annual maturities within twenty years commencing within five years, signed by the presiding commissioner and attested by the county clerk.

headings.title: Bond sale by county treasurer and non-county obligation
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history note. Covers delivery to and sale by the county treasurer as deemed necessary by the commission at not less than ninety-five cents on the dollar plus accrued interest, face-of-bond purpose statement, payment from sections 243.550 to 243.553 assessments, and explicit exclusion of county funds and county obligation.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read both subsections and history note (L. 1993 S.B. 56 § 243.560 subsecs. 1, 2) and verified all source and subsection fingerprints. Checked 90-percent sections 243.550 to 243.553 assessment cap, $100 minimum denominations, 6-percent semiannual interest, 5-year start and 20-year maturity limit, source phrasing 'convenient banking hours or trust company's office' ('hours' for 'house' retained), presiding commissioner/clerk execution, treasurer sale at 95-cent minimum plus accrued interest, and explicit non-county obligation clause. Retained both drafted titles as accurate.

headings.title: Advance assessment provisions, deficiency levies, and bond security
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history note (L. 1993 S.B. 56 § 243.560 subsecs. 4, 5). Requires the county commission to account in advance for maturing bonds and interest when making assessments, make additional benefit levies if sections 243.550 to 243.553 assessment proceeds are insufficient, and under no circumstances make an assessment impairing bond security or the payment fund.

headings.title: Exclusive use of bond sale proceeds
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history note. Restricts funds derived from bond sales exclusively to paying the cost of drainage works and improvements and authorized costs, expenses, fees, and salaries, and for no other purpose. Revised during review from 'Permitted use' to 'Exclusive use' to reflect the 'no other purpose' restriction.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read both subsections and history note (L. 1993 S.B. 56 § 243.560 subsecs. 4, 5) and verified all source and subsection fingerprints. Checked mandatory advance provision for maturing bonds and interest, additional benefit levies when sections 243.550 to 243.553 assessments are insufficient, strict nonimpairment of bond security/payment fund, and exclusive restriction of bond-sale proceeds to drainage works and authorized costs/expenses/fees/salaries ('and used for no other purpose'). Revised subsection 2 title from 'Permitted use' to 'Exclusive use' to capture the prohibition on other uses; retained subsection 1.
